uses.name: An independent second build of the design (catches spec errors)
uses.what: Because the Revit builder re-created walls, openings, stair and furniture from the spec with its own geometry kernel, errors in the spec's own geometry appeared as read-back mismatches. The Revit read-back post-conditions (U10, U11, U18) ran on the same spec and on what Revit built.
caught_or_delivered: Walls through the ramp, door under soffit, openings through columns, credited-but-unbuilt window, unglazed faces, missing approved details, hatch opening not located, stair vs column (see defects D01-D12).
uses.proposed_replacement: The built scene is not independent of the spec generator in the way a Revit rebuild was (villa_render consumes revit_spec). Independence must come from the checks measuring the scene meshes with a different method than the generator: occupancy/ray/face-plane tests, not re-running the same box functions. Proof: frozen historic geometry fails, D1 passes, and a mutation set of seeded defects in D1 is caught with reported recall.
uses.equivalence_proof: Seeded-defect recall on the real historic cases; no tuning of a failing check.

uses.name: Units and datum authority
uses.what: Revit fixed one project coordinate system shared with the CAD export, levels (B -1.80, GF +1.20, APT +4.20, ROOF) and the mm() boundary. The scene datum is GF FFL = 0 (B -3000), Revit's 1200 mm higher; the L2 model records both.
consumers: every stage that quotes a level or elevation
caught_or_delivered: 304.8x units class; 'B is -1.80 in Revit but -3000 in the scene' contract note (L2-model.md proposed contract change 1).
uses.proposed_replacement: A single levels table in contracts/model with a check that scene level planes (floor/ceiling/slab faces) sit at the table's values.
uses.equivalence_proof: Scene face z-histogram peaks equal the level table; frozen env-readback levels equal the table.

uses.name: Holder of the client's existing-structure model (kept columns, framing, slabs, levels, grids, neighbours)
uses.what: omar.rvt is the only artefact holding the real kept structure with exact ids and sub-millimetre values (column face 3977.2 vs CAD 3977). The stair and opening checks ran against it through omar-env.rvt. After freezing, the pipeline depends on villa_env constants only.
caught_or_delivered: Revit held 3977.2; Python used 3977 and passed a clash the client structure would have had (LEARNINGS 700-706).
uses.proposed_replacement: Freeze with hashes; decide the tolerance policy (sub-mm datum differences) in the clash check. Re-opening the model needs Revit (or a client IFC/DWG).
uses.equivalence_proof: Frozen values reproduce Revit's 6-option intersection list (U12).

uses.equivalence_proof: U12 replay; seeded clashes.
